public_rationale: The claim has concrete supporting examples: a new pension-backed data center commitment, insurer involvement in compute financing, and a loan repaid from lease payments. These establish parts of the account. The reviewed records do not sufficiently establish the claimed increase across both funding sources or complete the link to the obligations those funds support. That is an evidence gap, not evidence that the claim is false.
limitations: Commitments, funded investments and guarantees are different forms of exposure.
The pension announcement covers hyperscale capacity serving both cloud and AI.
The insurer allocation in the news report rests on an unnamed source.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI data centers are increasingly funded with pension and insurance money that depends on these payments.

statement.excerpt: It’s easy to dismiss this entirely as “rich people problems,” but AI data centers are increasingly funded — both directly and through private credit — using pension and insurance funds that rely on these (theoretical) payments for future yield to pay out premiums.

our_interpretation: Use April through June 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter before the July 22 post for which financing announcements could already be public. Earlier periods provide comparison context.
The plain reading is expanding pension and insurer participation in AI data center financing, not a specified percentage share of all financing.
New commitments establish expanding participation but must be distinguished from deployed capital, guarantees and proposed transactions.

Read the reference to paying out premiums as meeting pension and insurance benefit obligations from portfolios that include these investments. It does not claim that an entire fund depends on one project.
This is a qualitative claim about financing sources, not a stated company financial amount; metric_scope is null.
criteria.support_condition: Dated records establish increasing pension and insurer participation through direct investment and private credit by the target quarter, and trace expected project payments into investments supporting beneficiary or policyholder obligations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records show that the asserted participation was absent or declining, or establish that the identified money and payment flows were not pension or insurance assets supporting those obligations.
